title: Fragmented keying analysis and TTL sweeper procedures for safe cache policy application
creator: Ava Chen
description: We need an end-to-end engineering deliverable that analyzes fragmented cache key shapes across representative workloads, builds a probabilistic hit-rate model for prefix TTL recommendation, and produces an automated 'sweeper' procedure to apply/rollback TTL and keying changes safely. The goal is to feed recommendations into the batching/caching advisor in Redwood Optimize and provide an operational playbook for staged application with safety gates.
background: Current KV prefix caching experiments show inconsistent hit-rate lifts between workloads. Some prefixes are fragmented (many low-frequency variants), causing TTL increases to waste cache capacity while others are undersized. Manual tuning by SREs has been slow and risk-prone. We also lack an automated safety sweep that can revert ineffective or harmful policy changes quickly.
proposal: 1) Instrument a sampling job that profiles live request prefixes and computes fragmentation metrics (distinct suffix cardinality, frequency skew, median inter-arrival). 2) Fit a lightweight probabilistic hit-rate model (Poisson+zipf hybrid) to predict marginal hit-rate gain versus TTL for each prefix shape. 3) Generate TTL recommendations with confidence intervals and expected cache cost delta. 4) Implement a TTL sweeper that applies changes in micro-batches (shadow dry-run -> staged canary -> progressive apply) with runtime safety checks (error budget, 99th latency, cache eviction churn). 5) Expose both per-prefix recommendation and global rollout plan to Redwood Optimize and Console for operator approval.
rollout_plan: Sampling job: 48h canonical sample across 3 customer workloads (hosted API high-throughput, dedicated reserved pool, private VPC).
Model training: run offline model on sampled data, produce per-prefix predicted hit curve and cost delta (2 days).
Dry-run shadow: apply TTL recommendations to shadow cache traffic for 12 hours, collect hit/miss and eviction metrics (1 day).
Canary: select 5% of prefixes ranked by expected economic impact where confidence interval < 10%; apply to 1% of traffic for 6 hours, monitor SLOs.
Progressive apply: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback triggers at each step.
acceptance_criteria: Sampling job produces stable prefix statistics and fragmentation buckets for all three workloads.
Probabilistic model returns predicted hit-rate gain and 90% CI for TTL deltas for >80% of active prefixes.
TTL sweeper implements dry-run, canary, progressive apply and automated rollback heuristics as documented.
Console shows recommendations with cost delta and suggested rollout plan; operator can approve or pause.
A safety run across staging demonstrates automated rollback triggers fire correctly on synthetic SLO regressions.
metrics: Predicted hit-rate delta vs observed hit-rate delta (per-prefix)
Cache footprint change (GB) and per-token cost delta
Rollback frequency and mean time to revert
Model confidence coverage (fraction of prefixes with CI width < threshold)
risks: Model miscalibration leading to widespread TTL increases that increase eviction churn and cost.
Fragmentation drift: sampling snapshot may not represent future traffic shapes, causing poor decisions.
Operational complexity: more frequent cache config changes could increase incident surface if not automated safely.
Edge customers on Private deployments might have restricted rollout windows; sweeper must support manual gating.
mitigations: Constrain initial recommendations to small TTL deltas and only high-confidence prefixes.
Require shadow dry-run validation and canary step before any traffic-affecting apply.
Implement automatic rollback triggers tied to SLOs, eviction rate thresholds, and cost anomalies.
Provide a staging-only evaluation mode for Private customers and an operator 'approve' step in Console.
test_plan: Unit tests for sampling ETL and fragmentation metrics calculation.
Synthetic workloads that emulate high-fragmentation, low-fragmentation, and bursty prefixes for integration tests.
Staging dry-run where TTL recommendations are applied to a secondary cache namespace and compared to baseline over 24h.
Chaos test: inject artificial latency/error during canary to validate rollback flow.
